node: Private-label coffee, tea, extracts, syrups, and beverage solutions
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: The cleanest public exposure is on the supply side: a few B2B coffee and beverage solution providers sit closest to restaurant and foodservice procurement. Customer-side exposure is concentrated in large coffee-heavy restaurant brands, but those are mostly reference anchors rather than pure-play beneficiaries. The underfollowed lane is led by small/mid-cap suppliers with customer concentration, leverage, and execution risk. Layer 1B expands the restaurant beverage-input node into a focused universe of US-listed suppliers with direct or second-order exposure to private-label coffee, tea, extracts, syrups, foodservice beverage programs, direct-store-delivery, roasting/extract capacity, and customer qualification. The most relevant underfollowed names are Farmer Brothers, Westrock Coffee, TreeHouse Foods, and Coffee Holding Co. The bottleneck thesis is operational rather than purely demand-driven: sourcing green coffee, roasting/extract capacity, DSD/service execution, customer retention, commodity pass-through, leverage, and working-capital durability. Expanded the underfollowed universe around B2B coffee, tea, extracts, private-label beverage manufacturing, foodservice distribution, and restaurant/c-store/hospitality channel exposure. The strongest direct public-company fits are Westrock Coffee, Farmer Bros., and Coffee Holding Co.; US Foods is included as a reference distributor/channel anchor rather than a pure-play beverage supplier. Key bottlenecks to verify in later layers are customer qualification, DSD or distributor reach, roasting/extract capacity, commodity coffee
